fatal_errors: The proposed single-phase/configurational-entropy mechanism conflicts with the target mechanism, in which uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases formed during high-temperature SPS mediate the improved properties.
The intervention omits spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C and instead changes alloy composition to induce a multiphase state, confounding composition with phase structure.
The specified tests miss the key conditions: oxidation at 900 °C in air, corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl, and comparison across 800–1000 °C sintering temperatures.
The baseline is a compositionally altered multiphase alloy rather than otherwise comparable samples sintered at lower temperatures.

No existing observations are supplied to support the hypothesis, and the falsification rule allows failure in one of the required property classes without falsifying the claimed combined-performance mechanism.
explanation: The response addresses the general lightweight-HEA property tradeoff and proposes measurable mechanical, electrochemical, and oxidation comparisons, so it is a testable alternative. However, it does not reconstruct the central processing–structure–property relation: MgAlTiVFeCo powder is SPS-consolidated, with the optimum at 1000 °C arising from high density and oxide barrier phases such as AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3. It also misses the reported parabolic, biphasic oxidation kinetics, passive-film/Cl− exclusion mechanism, quantitative density and hardness outcomes, electrochemical values, and the 800–1000 °C processing boundary associated with insufficient densification and Mg volatilization. Its generic entropy-stabilized single-phase account is plausible in principle but unsupported here and mechanistically opposite to the target evidence.
